scope: Existing native Map title list/selection, World relay, original gold-title learning transitions, fresh/full-graph persistence and recovery. Not complete title awards or gameplay.

source.finding: List Bow/main/tutorial gates; owned/different selection only; no tutorial gate on selection
Title selection calls World and asynchronous base save; gold promotion precedes owned-title early return, and gained rows share selected flag
Original title list, gain and change response field order
Title row persistence and transfer keep flags; exact World relay layout; base-save ignores title argument
Load/transfer accepts multiple selected rows, last assignment wins; World applies selection to replicas and primary notifies neighboring cells
TTITLETABLE load has no ORDER BY; TSaveCharTitle persists id/flag
Title updates World character and fans out to every Map, including origin
Client title list/gain semantics and selected-title nameplate/UI update

wire.TITLELIST_ACK: 0x54f5, BYTE count then WORD id/BYTE selected, ascending unsigned IDs
wire.CHANGECHARBASE_ACK: 0x544a, BYTE result=0, DWORD char, BYTE kind=103, BYTE value=0, int32 byte-count/name bytes, WORD title, DWORD seconds=0
wire.World: Original MW_CHANGECHARBASE_ACK/REQ body: DWORD char/key, BYTE kind/value, WORD title, int32/name bytes; no added nonce or fields

preserved_quirks: Same current ID or unowned ID is silent; Bow is silent; tutorial gate only on list
GetTitle promotes live selected ID before early return on any eligible owned title, without necessarily changing persisted flags
All gained gold titles can share selected=true; runtime may temporarily name an absent title until client selects a gained title
Original reload/transfer re-derives live selected ID from saved/transferred flags; a transient gold promotion can therefore disappear on relogin
modern_differences: Selection flags, append receipt and checkpoint commit before World publication; replaces separate asynchronous legacy persistence and gives pipelined requests a durable linearization point
Registered ready primary and exact session key/connection authorize relay; replicas do not persist or broadcast
Malformed request bodies are rejected instead of permissive reads; duplicate IDs/over-width lists fail closed
Native SQL hydration uses unsigned ascending ID order and last selected wins; legacy SELECT lacked ORDER BY
Delayed primary World echoes only publish notifications: they do not reapply old state over a newer commit; exact-connection FIFO suppresses unsolicited/duplicate echoes
Pending World notifications are bound to the local authority epoch; same-socket promotion clears predecessor queue entries, and non-primary/transfer phases discard abandoned echoes.
verified_scenarios: PostgreSQL fresh and complete-graph title selection, one concurrent winner, stale selection/purchase/save fences, replica/epoch/generation rejection
Same/unowned silent requests, selecting owned no-title0, gold live-ID vs flag divergence, fresh/full-graph relogin
Late SQL failure rolls flags and append receipt back; actual TCP closes without success; successful selection after removing known rollback
Actual original-format encrypted Login/Map and plain World relay, independent Python oracle for all response bytes and flag state
Map SIGKILL/restart re-derives selected ID and does not replay accepted purchases
Controlled seven-socket audience test: three-by-three cells, map/channel boundaries, FIFO delayed echoes, invalid/duplicate echo suppression, replica projection without primary broadcast
World transport test: exact all-Map body, primary/replica distinction, key/shape/unregistered rejection
32 pure source arithmetic/gate/title/wire checks in existing skill-learning suite
Controlled same-socket successor epoch and non-primary notification discard regression; production transfer/failure acceptance remains separately scoped.
remaining: Complete title awards/resets and achievement dependencies; complete trainer, skill and gameplay scope in capability matrix
Original EXE, matching data and runnable client unavailable; source TVERSION 0x2918 alone is not a supported binary build
No original-client visual/timing acceptance, including pipelined title selection versus skill learning

Title-specific fault at every point between successful DB commit and World echo, and complete multi-neighbor churn, are not claimed tested; existing broader World-loss/primary-transfer tests remain bounded
Full arbitrary malformed/multi-selected historical title corpus not available; synthetic states and source contracts are distinguished from production acceptance
